comments.text:
The following program results in a segfault:

```
> wilcox.test(1:855555, 5:12, exact = TRUE)

 *** caught segfault ***
address 0xe256bf5e21e8, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: .dwilcox(s, m, n, z)
 2: .pwilcox(q, n.x, n.y, z)
 3: .wilcox_test_two_pval_exact(STAT, n.x, n.y, alternative)
 4: wilcox.test.default(1:855555, 5:12, exact = TRUE)
 5: wilcox.test(1:855555, 5:12, exact = TRUE)
An irrecoverable exception occurred. R is aborting now ...
[1]    2718 segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

Reproducible by running, regular build, no special build configuration:
```
R -e 'wilcox.test(1:855555, 5:12, exact = TRUE)'
```

Version:
```
svn rev r90590
```

OS:
```
Linux Ubuntu 26.04, x86
```

Also reproduced on arm64 Ubuntu and M1 Mac.

comments.text:
setting a breakpoint for dpermdist2 via gdb reveals a case of (32 bit) integer overflow...

Breakpoint 1, dpermdist2 (x=0x5555578ed1d8, m=0x555557a8a338) at permdist.c:53
53	SEXP dpermdist2(SEXP x, SEXP m) {
(gdb) until 52

Program received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
0x00007ffff41c50b5 in dpermdist2 (x=<optimized out>, m=<optimized out>)
    at permdist.c:90
90	            dH[idx + j] = 0.0;
(gdb) print n
$5 = 855563
(gdb) print sum_a
$6 = 855555
(gdb) print sum_b
$7 = 1844462140
(gdb) print (size_t)(sum_a + 1) * (size_t)(sum_b + 1)
$8 = 1578040651505396

Both sum_a and sum_bp1 are standard 32-bit signed integers; in this case their product exceeds INT_MAX.

Since exact permutation distributions for a sample size this large are computationally intractable, it would make sense to have wilcox.text reject such tables and error out with a recommendation to use exact = FALSE.

Or use 64-bit casting on line 86 of src/library/stats/src/permdist.c:

size_t total_elements = (size_t)(sum_a + 1) * (size_t)sum_bp1;
dH = (double*) R_alloc(total_elements, sizeof(double));

which should cause R to cleanly throw a vector memory exhausted error, rather than segfaulting.

comments.creator: ikrylov
